lines: Called by the seat-fixing word: three seats —
breath-wind, frame, without — breath's rule first.
Count the coming course breath-abiding;
its count, in rank and off, is time —
gleaming in the Highest alone, the God's might Kālī;
sundered, its show in rank and off is breath-sway.
sanskrit_cite: sa eva sthānaprakalpanaśabdena uktaḥ tatra tridhā sthānaṃ prāṇavāyuḥ śarīraṃ bāhyaṃ ca tatra prāṇe tāvat vidhiḥ sarvaḥ asau vakṣyamāṇaḥ adhvā prāṇasthaḥ kalyate tasya kramākramakalanaiva kālaḥ sa ca parameśvara eva antarbhāti tadbhāsanaṃ ca devasya kālī nāma śaktiḥ bhedena tu tadābhāsanaṃ kramākramayoḥ prāṇavṛttiḥ

lines: Sheer knowing sets a shape apart from knowns;
hemmed, hence going knowable: the void.
Then, free, swooping the thing with clutching zest,
deed-mighty, breath-shaped, life-natured —
filling the frame five-formed, it gleams as if awake.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvid eva hi prameyebhyo vibhaktaṃ rūpaṃ gṛhṇāti ata eva ca avacchedayogāt vedyatāṃ yāntī nabhaḥ tataḥ svātantryāt meye svīkārautsukyena nipatantī kriyāśaktipradhānā prāṇanārūpā jīvasvabhāvā pañcabhī rūpaiḥ dehaṃ yataḥ pūrayati tato 'sau cetana iva bhāti

lines: In power, deed is time's road; east and north
the place-road wears motley shapes;
there letter-spell-word roads stand in time's road —
beyond the fine, the gross in form.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kriyā śaktau kālādhvā prācyabhāge uttare tu mūrtivaicitryarūpo deśādhvā tatra varṇamantrapadādhvanaḥ kālādhvani sthitiḥ parasūkṣmasthūlarūpatvāt

lines: But the place-road's stand, soul-ray-natured —
so shall be in its own stead.
sanskrit_cite: deśādhvasthitis tu tattvapurakalātmanā iti bhaviṣyati svāvasare

lines: Though in the frame, warp-and-woof without-within, is breath —
yet plain-felt striving starts at the heart —
hence from there alone declare it.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yady api dehe sabāhyābhyantaram otaprotarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ tathāpi prasphuṭasaṃvedyaprayatnaḥ asau hṛdayāt prabhṛti iti tata eva ayaṃ nirūpaṇīyaḥ

lines: Lord-might, self-might, push — a triple
pricks the breath to run, by minor-major modes.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prabhuśaktiḥ ātmaśaktiḥ yatna iti tritayaṃ prāṇeraṇe hetuḥ guṇamukhyabhāvāt

lines: Heart to twelve's-end, by own fingers, thirty-six
the breath-road runs, out and in, each fitly thewed.
sanskrit_cite: tatra hṛdayāt dvādaśāntāntaṃ svāṅgulaiḥ sarvasya ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaḥ prāṇacāraḥ nirgame praveśe ca svocitabalayatnadehatvāt sarvasya

lines: Water-clock, moon-day, month, year, year-thronged —
whole time is told out in breath.
Bean-and-fifth the measure — hence dawns the clock;
sixty beans the clock, seventy-two long.
sanskrit_cite: tatra ghaṭikā tithiḥ māso varṣaṃ ca varṣasamūhātmā iti samastaḥ kālaḥ parisamāpyate tatra sapañcāṃśe aṅgule caṣaka iti sthityā ghaṭikodayaḥ ghaṭikā hi ṣaṣṭyā caṣakaiḥ tasmāt dvāsaptatyaṅgulā bhavati

lines: Now the moon-day's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atha tithyudayaḥ

lines: Two fingers and a quarter, a wink; four winks a watch;
half-winks either end the gloaming — out-breath day, in-breath night.
sanskrit_cite: sapādam aṅguladvayaṃ tuṭiḥ ucyate tāsu catasṛṣu praharaḥ tuṭyardhaṃ tuṭyardhaṃ tatra saṃdhyā evaṃ nirgame dinaṃ praveśe rātriḥ iti tithyudayaḥ

lines: Now the month's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atha māsodayaḥ

lines: Day the dark half, night the bright;
first and last half-winks unclocked rest —
the mid fifteen alone are days, light and rest day-night.
sanskrit_cite: tatra dinaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaḥ rātriḥ śuklaḥ tatra pūrvaṃ tuṭyardham antyaṃ ca tuṭyardhaṃ viśrāntiḥ akālakalitāḥ madhyās tu pañcadaśa tuṭaya eva tithayaḥ tatra prakāśo viśrāntiś ca iti ete eva dinaniśe

lines: Knowable's glow is day; its melt in the melter, night;
they — glow and rest, quick-slow, in endless else, in sameness still.
sanskrit_cite: tatra vedyamayatāprakāśo dinaṃ vedyasya vicārayitari layo rātriḥ te ca prakāśaviśrāntī cirāciravaicitryāt anantabhede tatsāmye tu viṣuvat

lines: In dark half the in-breath moon fattens digit by digit
till on the fifteenth, by the twelve-end, the thinned moon
melts into breath-sun alone.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣe prāṇārke apānacandra āpyāyikām ekām ekāṃ kalām arpayati yāvat pañcadaśyāṃ tuṭau dvādaśāntasamīpe kṣīṇapṛthagbhūtakalāprasaraḥ candramāḥ prāṇārka eva līyate

lines: Straightway, the half-wink: the fortnight's hinge.
sanskrit_cite: tadanantaraṃ yat tuṭyardhaṃ sa pakṣasaṃdhiḥ

lines: Its east half new-moon, second first-day.
sanskrit_cite: tasya ca tuṭyardhasya prācyam ardham āmāvasyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prātipadam

lines: On first-day, in that part, when through tithi's cut it slips —
then the grip. There Rāhu, twin with thing-moon,
unmelting, mere covering, quaffs the sun-gone moon-dew.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prātipade tasmin bhāge sa āmāvasyo bhāgo yadā kāsaprayatnāvadhānādikṛtāt tithicchedāt viśati tadā tatra grahaṇam tatra ca vedyarūpasomasahabhūto māyāpramātṛrāhuḥ svabhāvatayā vilāpanāśaktaḥ kevalam ācchādanamātrasamarthaḥ sūryagataṃ cāndram amṛtaṃ pibati iti

lines: Since it makes the three unparted, holy time, otherworld-fruiting.
sanskrit_cite: pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatritayāvibhāgakāritvāt sa puṇyaḥ kālaḥ pāralaukikaphalapradaḥ

lines: Then in-breath the knowing-sun brims digit by digit the in-breath moon
till the fifteenth wink is full — then hinge and grip as before —
but this-world-fruiting: so the month's rise.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ praviśati prāṇe cidarka ekaikayā kalayā apānacandram āpūrayati yāvat pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ pūrṇimā tadanantaraṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ grahaṇaṃ ca iti prāgvat etat tu aihikaphalapradam iti māsodayaḥ

lines: Now the year's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atha varṣodayaḥ

lines: Dark fortnight alone the northward road; six by six fingers the crossing, Ram to Twins' end.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣa eva uttarāyaṇaṃ ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu aṅguleṣu saṃkrāntiḥ makarāt mithunāntām

lines: Five days a finger, day-night parted too;
in-drawn, the southward road — womb-hood, birth-ache,
not-yet-born, shall-be-born, birth's start, being-born,
birth-and-sixfold change, Ram onward in rank.
sanskrit_cite: tatra pratyaṅgulaṃ pañca tithayaḥ tatrāpi dinarātrivibhāgaḥ evaṃ praveśe dakṣiṇāyanaṃ garbhatvam udbhavecchā udbubhūṣutā udbhaviṣyatvam udbhavārambhaḥ udbhavattā janmādivikāraṣaṭkaṃ ca iti kramāt makarādiṣu iti

lines: So praised here bears meet fruit.
sanskrit_cite: tathaiva upāsā atra phalaṃ samucitaṃ karoti

lines: Ram's sire to grandsire, Rudras and their Rays — twelve wardens: so the year's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atra ca dakṣādyāḥ pitāmahāntā rudrāḥ śaktayaś ca dvādaśādhipataya iti varṣodayaḥ

lines: Sixty days a finger — a year at each crossing;
in-out, twelve-year dawn; three hundred days a finger-and-fifth — a year
where once the bean was named — by count five years a crossing;
so in one out-in breath sixty-year dawn —
one-and-twenty thousand six hundred days.
sanskrit_cite: pratyaṅgulaṃ ṣaṣṭiḥ tithaya iti krameṇa saṃkrāntau varṣam ity anena krameṇa praveśanirgamayoḥ dvādaśābdodayaḥ pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ śatatrayaṃ sapañcāṃśe 'ṅgule varṣaṃ yatra prāk caṣakam uktam iti gaṇanayā saṃkrāntau pañca varṣāṇi iti anayā paripāṭyā ekasmin prāṇanirgamapraveśakāle ṣaṣṭyabdodayaḥ atra ekaviṃśatisahasrāṇi ṣaṭ śatāni iti tithīnāṃ saṃkhyā

lines: That number alone the day-night breath-tell;
beyond sixty-year dawn none pries, for no end.
sanskrit_cite: tāvatī eva ahorātre prāṇasaṃkhyā iti na ṣaṣṭyabdodayāt adhikaṃ parīkṣyate ānantyāt

lines: Man's year the gods' moon-day; twelve thousand god-years four ages.
sanskrit_cite: tatra mānuṣaṃ varṣaṃ devānāṃ tithiḥ anena krameṇa divyāni dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi caturyugam

lines: Four, three, two, one — from the full age on, hundredfold, eight gloamings.
sanskrit_cite: catvāri trīṇi dve ekam iti kṛtāt prabhṛti tāvadbhiḥ śataiḥ aṣṭau saṃdhyāḥ

lines: Seventy-one fours an aeon's lord; fourteen his day;
at day's end, worlds fire-burnt, worlds smoke-lulled,
all folk swift, flame-sped, in man's world ghost-pale stand.
sanskrit_cite: caturyugānām ekasaptatyā manvantaram manvantaraiḥ caturdaśabhiḥ brāhmaṃ dinaṃ brahmadinānte kālāgnidagdhe lokatraye anyatra ca lokatraye dhūmaprasvāpite sarve janā vegavad agnipreritā janaloke pralayākalībhūya tiṣṭhanti

lines: But the awaked — Cub-lord, Gold-lord and the rest — play in the high world.
sanskrit_cite: prabuddhās tu kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakeśādyā maholoke krīḍanti

lines: Then at night's close Brahmā's forth-pouring.
sanskrit_cite: tato niśāsamāptau brāhmī sṛṣṭiḥ

lines: By this rod a hundred years — Brahmā's life.
sanskrit_cite: anena mānena varṣaśataṃ brahmāyuḥ

lines: His day is Viṣṇu's; that long his night; his too a hundred life.
sanskrit_cite: tat viṣṇoḥ dinaṃ tāvatī ca rātriḥ tasyāpi śatam āyuḥ

lines: That day; above it hail, O Rudra-world's lord! —
Rudra's; that long the night; year as before; that hundred too the bound.
sanskrit_cite: tat dinaṃ tadūrdhve rudralokaprabho rudrasya tāvatī rātriḥ prāgvat varṣaṃ tacchatam api ca avadhiḥ

lines: At Rudra's close, godward going; his office-term told;
world-egg bearers' day; a hundred Rudras' night; theirs too a hundred life.
sanskrit_cite: tatra rudrasya tadavasitau śivatvagatiḥ rudrasya uktādhikārāvadhiḥ brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ tat dinaṃ śatarudrāṇāṃ niśā tāvatī teṣām api ca śatam āyuḥ

lines: When a hundred Rudras gutter out — the world-egg breaks.
sanskrit_cite: śatarudrakṣaye brahmāṇḍavināśaḥ

lines: From water-stuff to the Unshown, rank on rank, the Rudras' life.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jalatattvāt avyaktāntam etad eva krameṇa rudrāṇām āyuḥ

lines: The elder's life the younger's day.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvasyāyur uttarasya dinam iti

lines: Then Brahmā and Rudras, clean-officered, stand in the Unshown.
sanskrit_cite: tataś ca brahmā rudrāś ca abādyadhikāriṇaḥ avyakte tiṣṭhanti iti

lines: And then the Gracious-Throat, the withdrawer.
sanskrit_cite: śrīkaṇṭhanāthaś ca tadā saṃhartā

lines: Between-dissolve this; spent, forth-pouring.
sanskrit_cite: eṣo 'vāntarapralayaḥ tatkṣaye sṛṣṭiḥ

lines: Other writs, though told, are poured as well.
sanskrit_cite: tatra śāstrāntaram uktā api sṛjyante

lines: But the Throat-lord's own life — the sheath-Rudras' day, that long the night;
their life — Gloaming's day, that long alone the night;
and in her the all in Māyā melts away entire.
sanskrit_cite: yat tu śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya svam āyuḥ tat kañcukavāsināṃ rudrāṇāṃ dinaṃ tāvatī rajanī teṣāṃ yad āyuḥ tat gahaneśadinaṃ tāvatī eva kṣapā tasyāṃ ca samastam eva māyāyāṃ vilīyate

lines: Once more Gloaming pours.
sanskrit_cite: punaḥ gahaneśaḥ sṛjati

lines: So take unshown time, ten half-highests folded, and speak Māyā's day — that long the night.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yaḥ avyaktakālaḥ taṃ daśabhiḥ parārdhaiḥ guṇayitvā māyādinaṃ kathayet tāvatī rātriḥ

lines: That alone is unmaking.
sanskrit_cite: sa eva pralayaḥ

lines: Māyā-time hundredfold in half-highests: a day in the Lord's plane.
sanskrit_cite: māyākālaḥ parārdhaśatena guṇita aiśvaratattve dinam

lines: Here breath pours the world, that long the night;
where breath hushes — in breath and in Brahma's cave-abode, in the hush — what knowing? — sequence there too.
sanskrit_cite: atra prāṇo jagat sṛjati tāvatī rātriḥ yatra prāṇapraśamaḥ prāṇe ca brahmabiladhāmni śānte 'pi yā saṃvit tatrāpy asti kramaḥ

lines: In the Lord's time hundredfold, the count thereof: the Blest day, that long the night; that alone the Great Unmaking.
sanskrit_cite: aiśvare kāle parārdhaśataguṇite yā saṃkhyā tat sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ tāvatī niśā sa eva mahāpralayaḥ

lines: The Blest, when his time ends, mounting drop, half-moon, checked,
melts in hum; hum in Might; that in the All-spread; she in the Unheld.
sanskrit_cite: sadāśivaḥ svakālaparikṣaye bindvardhacandranirodhikā ākramya nāde līyate nādaḥ śaktitattve tat vyāpinyāṃ sā ca anāśrite

lines: By Might-time ten-million-half-highest-fold: the Unheld's day.
sanskrit_cite: śaktikālena parārdhakoṭiguṇitena anāśritadinam

lines: The Unheld in the likeminded seat — which, that likeness, evenness; that, Brahma.
sanskrit_cite: anāśritaḥ sāmanase pade yat tat sāmanasyaṃ sāmyaṃ tat brahma

lines: From this likeness, the unlimbed, from time — by a wink's measure —
rises the told wheel-whirl of all time's outgoing and indrawing.
sanskrit_cite: asmāt sāmanasyāt akalyāt kālāt nimeṣonmeṣamātratayā proktāśeṣakālaprasarapravilayacakrabhramodayaḥ

lines: One, ten, hundred, thousand, myriad, lakh, crore, ten-crore, hundred-crore, thousand-crore, lakh-crore, ten-lakh-crore, ocean, end, midst, half-highest —
so tenfold in rank, eighteen: the count-law.
sanskrit_cite: ekaṃ daśa śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ lakṣaṃ niyutaṃ koṭiḥ arbudaṃ vṛndaṃ kharvaṃ nikharvaṃ padmaṃ śaṅkuḥ samudram antyaṃ madhyam parārdham iti krameṇa daśaguṇitāni aṣṭādaśa iti gaṇitavidhiḥ

lines: So numberless forth-pourings and in-pullings in one great-pouring-shaped breath —
it too in knowing, she in the adjunct, it in bare awareness —
of bare awareness alone this throb called time-rise.
sanskrit_cite: evam asaṃkhyāḥ sṛṣṭipralayāḥ ekasmin mahāsṛṣṭirūpe prāṇe so 'pi saṃvidi sā upādhau sa cinmātre cinmātrasyaiva ayaṃ spando yad ayaṃ kālodayo nāma

lines: Thence alone dream-weave and the rest vary, yet jar not.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva svapnasaṃkalpādau vaicitryam asya na virodhāvaham

lines: As in out-breath time's rise, so in in-breath too, heart to root-seat's bound.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yathā prāṇe kālodayaḥ tathā apāne 'pi hṛdayāt mūlapīṭhaparyantam

lines: As in heart, throat, palate, brow, cleft, twelve's-end the six — Brahmā, Pervader, Roarer, Lord, the Blest, the Unheld —
so in in-breath too, in heart-bud bliss-wane-wax twelve's-ends:
child, youth, age, rebirth, release — these wardens.
sanskrit_cite: yathā ca hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivānāśritākhyaṃ kāraṇaṣaṭkam tathaiva apāne 'pi hṛtkandānandasaṃkocavikāsadvādaśānteṣu bālyayauvanavārddhakanidhanapunarbhavamuktyadhipataya ete

lines: Now in the even breath time's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atha samāne kālodayaḥ

lines: The even breath roving ten heart-tubes wafts saps evenly through all the frame;
there roving the eight airts, it apes as it were the knowers' regents' play.
sanskrit_cite: samāno hārdīṣu daśāsu nāḍīṣu saṃcaran samaste dehe sāmyena rasādīn vāhayati tatra digaṣṭake saṃcaran taddikpaticeṣṭām iva pramātuḥ anukārayati

lines: Up-down straying three tubes it plies to and fro.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvādhas tu saṃcaran tisṛṣu nāḍīṣu gatāgataṃ karoti

lines: There on level-day, without, at dawn, a clock and quarter the mid-path bears.
sanskrit_cite: tatra viṣuvaddine bāhye prabhātakāle sapādāṃ ghaṭikāṃ madhyamārge vahati

lines: Then nine hundred breath-tosses — by count, without, two clocks and a half — left, right, left, right, left — five crossings.
sanskrit_cite: tato navaśatāni prāṇavikṣepāṇām iti gaṇanayā bahiḥ sārdhaghaṭikādvayaṃ vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme iti pañca saṃkrāntayaḥ

lines: Then, five crossings past, in thirteen-and-three-quarter clocks gone by,
at southern harvest noon, nine hundred breaths.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ saṃkrāntipañcake vṛtte pādonāsu caturdaśasu ghaṭikāsu atikrāntāsu dakṣiṇaṃ śāradaṃ viṣuvanmadhyāhne nava prāṇaśatāni

lines: Then too right, left, right, left, right — five crossings, nine hundred apiece —
so by night as well.
sanskrit_cite: tato 'pi dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe iti saṃkrāntipañcakaṃ pratyekaṃ navaśatāni ity evaṃ rātrāv api iti

lines: So on level-day and its night, twelve and twelve crossings.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ viṣuvaddivase tadrātrau ca dvādaśa dvādaśa saṃkrāntayaḥ

lines: Then as days wax and wane, crossings wax and wane.
sanskrit_cite: tato dinavṛddhikṣayeṣu saṃkrāntivṛddhikṣayaḥ

lines: So in one even-breath gale two years, breath in-out unwed.
sanskrit_cite: evam ekasmin samānamaruti varṣadvayaṃ śvāsapraśvāsayogābhāvāt

lines: Here too twelve-year dawn and the rest as before.
sanskrit_cite: atrāpi dvādaśābdodayādi pūrvavat

lines: But in up-breath the course twelve-end-bound, of throb-natured time.
sanskrit_cite: udāne tu dvādaśāntāvadhiś cāraḥ spandamātrātmanaḥ kālasya

lines: Here too as before the rule.
sanskrit_cite: atrāpi pūrvavat vidhiḥ

lines: But in all-breath, for it spreads everywhere, even rankless, by fine upsurge — time's rise.
sanskrit_cite: vyāne tu vyāpakatvāt akrame 'pi sūkṣmocchalattāyogena kālodayaḥ

lines: Now the letter's rise.
sanskrit_cite: atha varṇodayaḥ

lines: There half-watch by half-watch the tribes rise level at the crossing;
of letter, of letter, two hundred sixteen breaths; without, thirty-six beans:
so the rise, unstriven letter-rise.
sanskrit_cite: tatra ardhaprahare ardhaprahare vargodayo viṣuvati samaḥ varṇasya varṇasya dve śate ṣoḍaśādhike prāṇānām bahiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat caṣakāṇi iti udayaḥ ayam ayatnajo varṇodayaḥ

lines: But striven is spell-rise: like the water-wheel's draw,
by one-pointed tending — wondrous spell-rise plied day and night —
with the spell's goddess one-ness wins.
sanskrit_cite: yatnajas tu mantrodayaḥ araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravāhanavat ekānusaṃdhibalāt citraṃ mantrodayaṃ divāniśam anusaṃdadhat mantradevatayā saha tādātmyam eti

lines: There in the ever-risen, by breath-count alone is rise-count told;
double it, halve it, and so by rank; in the eight-plus-hundred wheel two hundred rise.
So by rank, in gross and fine, in the rested one's road-form —
breath thinned, time devoured come true —
whole, one, just this knowing, wonder-mighty, shines.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sadodite prāṇacārasaṃkhyayaiva udayasaṃkhyā vyākhyātā taddviguṇite tadardham ityādi krameṇa aṣṭottaraśate cakre dviśata udayaḥ iti krameṇa sthūlasūkṣme cārasvarūpe viśrāntasya prāṇacāre kṣīṇe kālagrāse vṛtte sampūrṇām ekam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ citraśaktinirbharaṃ bhāsate

lines: Time-part alone parts knowing, not thing-part —
as hilltop-knowing stands.
Knowing's long-abiding — that alone the wink;
in one breath-rise one knowing, needs must —
and this: else never a single notion-knowing could be,
since word-stained in rank, since ranked even the measure.
sanskrit_cite: kālabheda eva saṃvedanabhedakaḥ na vedyabhedaḥ śikharasthajñānavat jñānasya yāvān avasthitikālaḥ sa eva kṣaṇaḥ prāṇodaye ca ekasmin ekam eva jñānam avaśyaṃ caitat anyathā vikalpajñānam ekaṃ na kiṃcit syāt kramikaśabdārūṣitatvāt mātrāyā api kramikatvāt

lines: Which once said: the high, the half-brief — so.
sanskrit_cite: yad āha tasyādita udāttam ardhahrasvam iti

lines: Till the between-throb dawns not, so long knowing alone.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt spandāntaraṃ yāvat na uditaṃ tāvat ekam eva jñānam

lines: Hence very eighty-one, when word-remembering, through manifold in-going —
that one, the Highest-aimed notion, by time-devoured,
unnotioned-natured alone results.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva ekāśīti padasmaraṇasamaye vividhadharmānupraveśamukhena eka eva asau parameśvaraviṣayo vikalpaḥ kālagrāse na avikalpātmā eva sampadyate iti

lines: So seeing all time's road in breath-rise alone,
and the sundry countless pourings and in-pullings, marking them there,
by self alone his lordship knowing — freed alone he comes to be.
sanskrit_cite: evam akhilaṃ kālādhvānaṃ prāṇodaya eva paśyan sṛṣṭisaṃhārāṃś ca vicitrān niḥsaṃkhyān tatraiva ākalayan ātmana eva pārameśvaryaṃ pratyabhijānan mukta eva bhavati iti

lines: Seeing his knowing-formed self's breath-might,
the shape faring there and past-time withal,
with forth-stand-back wheels ever-yoked — Bhairavī-state attains.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvidrūpasyātmanaḥ prāṇaśaktiṃ paśyan rūpaṃ tatragaṃ cātikālam sākaṃ sṛṣṭisthemasaṃhāracakrair nityodyukto bhairavībhāvam eti
